test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-4) Official paper (Held On: 10 May 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Ruchira was supposed to complete a task in 22 days. However, during the first 10 days she did only (1)/(30) of the work on each day. What share of the work will Ruchira have to do daily from the 11th day so that the work is completed on time?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Work done in first **10 days** = 10 × (1/30) = 1/3

Remaining work to be completed = 1 − 1/3 = 2/3

Remaining time available = 22 − 10 = **12 days**

Daily share of work required = (2/3) ÷ 12 = 1/18

**∴ The correct answer is 1/18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total duration = **22 days**

Daily work (Day 1 to 10) = 1/30

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/747fe90b4b02d21ffd35c05e01fcd3c20b119b99fc209b485966b192991724dc.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total work done in the first **10 days** = 10 × (1/30) = 1/3

⇒ Remaining work to be done = 1 − 1/3 = 2/3

⇒ Number of days remaining to finish the task = 22 − 10 = **12 days**

⇒ Daily work share required for the remaining period = (Remaining Work) ÷ (Remaining Days)

⇒ Daily work share = (2/3) ÷ 12

⇒ Daily work share = 2 / (3 × 12)

⇒ Daily work share = 2 / 36 = 1/18

**∴ The correct answer is 1/18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Concept of Work Rate

The **rate of work** is defined as the amount of work completed per unit of time. If a person completes a task in 'n' days, their daily work rate is 1/n.

Work-Time Relation

Total Work = **Time** × **Efficiency** (or Rate). For multi-phase tasks, Total Work = Sum of (Rateᵢ × Timeᵢ).

Remaining Work Calculation

When a fraction 'f' of work is completed, the **remaining work** is always (1 − f). This is crucial for planning resources to meet deadlines.</p
